mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30 months (p > 0.1) during tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of such labor weakening events (rolling IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% from the prior month is a leading indicator of consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during housing expansion phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects contracting business activity and reduced earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of INDPRO contraction periods (rolling IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as the Fed may pause or reverse hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) during such inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a decline in manufacturing payrolls (not directly observable but implied by INDPRO) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to weak labor demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while INDPRO continues downward trend
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with the trigger in 80% of episodes (Pearson IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month is a strong demand signal that drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in >60% of such episodes (rolling IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over 4 consecutive months suggests structural supply-side weakness, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day returns regardless of trigger.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (IC > 0.2 across all such contractions).
